note: Bit patterns are the normative fields; decimal fields are for reading and are emitted only for units of 32 values or fewer. This file carries no version strings so that regenerating it must reproduce it byte-for-byte; the interpreter and NumPy versions are printed to stderr by the generator and recorded in .plan/evidence/QM-0120.md.

cases.name: minus_one_zero_one_int8_symmetric
cases.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 1. s = max|g|/127 = 1/127; -1 -> -127, 0 -> 0, 1 -> 127; the round trip is exact because each input IS a code times s.

cases.name: tenths_int4_asymmetric
cases.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 2. None of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 is exact in f32, and that decides the answer: (f32(0.3) - f32(0.1)) rounds UP to a tie-to-even, so s is slightly larger than 0.2/15 and -f32(0.1)/s is -7.4999998 rather than -7.5. z is therefore -7, not the -8 that exact decimal arithmetic would give. The reconstructed minimum then sits BELOW 0.1 and the reconstructed maximum below 0.3, because the grid is offset by the rounding of z itself. Correct per §3.1; not an off-by-one.

cases.name: all_zero_int8_symmetric
cases.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 3 and §3.1's first degenerate row: s = 1, every code 0, output all zero, no division by zero and no NaN.

cases.name: all_zero_int8_asymmetric
cases.why: The same degenerate row under the asymmetric formula, where the scale is (max-min)/(n-1) and max == min.

cases.name: constant_ones_int4_asymmetric
cases.why: Zero dynamic range, non-zero: an all-ones norm weight. s = |1| = 1, z = rint(-1/1) = -1, so every value reconstructs bit-exactly. Note that s = 1 and s = |c| coincide at c = 1, which is exactly why this case alone cannot verify the rule -- see the three that follow.

cases.name: constant_half_int4_asymmetric
cases.why: The case that pins the zero-dynamic-range rule. s = |0.5| = 0.5, z = rint(-0.5/0.5) = -1, q = clamp(rint(1) + (-1), 0, 15) = 0, x̂ = (0 - (-1))*0.5 = 0.5 bit-exactly. Under the s = 1 rule this reconstructs to 0.0 -- a silent 100% error on a constant tensor.

cases.name: constant_negative_three_tenths_int8_asymmetric
cases.why: The negative sign of the same rule, and the one that pins z. s = |-0.3| = f32(0.3), z = rint(0.3/0.3) = +1, q = clamp(rint(-1) + 1, 0, 255) = 0, x̂ = (0 - 1)*0.3 = -0.3 bit-exactly. Under the s = 1 rule this also reconstructs to 0.0.

cases.name: constant_irrational_int4_asymmetric
cases.why: A constant with no short binary expansion, at both zero points, to show the two modes now agree. Under the s = 1 rule this reconstructs to 1.0 -- a 41% error in the WRONG direction.

cases.name: constant_irrational_int4_symmetric
cases.why: The symmetric counterpart of the case above: s = |0.823457|/7, q = 7, x̂ = 7*s = 0.823457. Symmetric was always exact here, and the two modes disagreeing on a constant tensor was the tell.

cases.name: constant_f32_max_int8_asymmetric
cases.why: The largest magnitude f32 holds, as a constant unit. s = |c| = f32::MAX, z = -1, code 0, x̂ = 1*s = f32::MAX bit-exactly -- no overflow, because the reachable code is 0 rather than 255. The SYMMETRIC path at the same magnitude does overflow and is refused; see `reconstruction_overflows_to_infinity_int8_symmetric`.

cases.name: constant_negative_f32_max_int4_symmetric
cases.why: int4 symmetric at -f32::MAX: s = |c|/7 and the reachable code is -7, so 7*s stays finite where int8's 127*s would not. Bit-exact.

cases.name: large_but_valid_zero_point_int8_asymmetric
cases.why: The only case that exercises the i64 -> f32 conversion in `(q - z).astype(F32)`. A huge offset with a two-ULP range gives z = 1687448320, which FITS in i32 (unlike the one-ULP version, which overflows and is refused), so |q - z| > 2^24 and the conversion ROUNDS. Every other accepted case has |z| <= 8, where the conversion is exact. If Rust's `i64 as f32` and NumPy's int64->float32 disagreed on ties, this is the case that would show it.

cases.name: constant_large_negative_int8_asymmetric
cases.why: A constant at -4e9, which the s = 1 rule REFUSED because it needed z = rint(4e9), outside i32. Under s = |c| the zero point is -(-1) = 1 and the unit reconstructs exactly, so no refusal is needed. The zero-point-overflow path is still reachable and still tested -- see the refusal `zero_point_outside_i32_int8_asymmetric`.

cases.name: exactly_representable_int8_symmetric
cases.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 7 and acceptance criterion 7: every input is already a multiple of s = 4/127, so the round trip is idempotent and bit-exact.

cases.name: boundary_halves_scale_one_int8_symmetric
cases.why: Acceptance criterion 2's rounding boundaries fed through simulate with s = 1 exactly: 0.5 -> 0, 1.5 -> 2, -0.5 -> -0, 2.5 -> 2. Half-away-from-zero would give 1, 2, -1, 3 and disagree on three of four.

cases.name: clamping_boundaries_int4_symmetric
cases.why: Acceptance criterion 2's clamping boundaries: params derived elsewhere (s = 1) applied to a unit that overshoots the int4 code range, so +9 clamps to +7 and -12 clamps to -8. This is the per-tensor and per-channel case -- the unit does not set its own scale.

cases.name: clamping_boundaries_int4_asymmetric
cases.why: The asymmetric clamp: q = clamp(rint(x/s) + z, 0, 15) with s = 1, z = 8, so x = 8 clamps at the top and x = -9 clamps at the bottom.

cases.name: mixed_signs_int8_asymmetric
cases.why: A realistic asymmetric unit whose range straddles zero, so z lands inside [0, 255] the way the textbook case does.

cases.name: mixed_signs_int4_symmetric
cases.why: int4 symmetric over the same values: 15 levels of headroom, so the reconstruction error is visible and the result is `quantized`, never `exact`.

cases.name: lcg_4096_int8_symmetric
cases.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 9: a 4096-element unit, the size q-quant must handle with allocation proportional to the unit and not to a 4096x4096 tensor.

cases.name: lcg_4096_int4_asymmetric
cases.why: The same 4096-element unit at the other extreme of the v1 surface.

grouped_cases.name: group_130_of_128_int8_symmetric
grouped_cases.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 6 and acceptance criterion 4: 130 values at group size 128 give two groups of 128 and 2. The final group is CLAMPED, never padded, so its scale comes from its own two values.

grouped_cases.name: group_130_of_128_int4_asymmetric
grouped_cases.why: The same clamped final group under the asymmetric formula, where a 2-element final group has its own zero point too.

grouped_cases.name: group_9_of_4_int4_symmetric
grouped_cases.why: A tiny non-dividing case that is legible by hand: 9 values at group size 4 give 4 + 4 + 1, and the 1-element final group is exactly representable at its own scale.

refusals.name: subnormal_scale_int8_symmetric
refusals.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 4: max|g| is the smallest f32 subnormal, so s = max|g|/127 underflows to zero. Refused, naming the unit.
refusals.detail: subnormal_scale_int8_symmetric derived scale 0.0, which is not a normal f32; quantising it would divide by zero or emit infinities

refusals.name: subnormal_scale_int4_asymmetric
refusals.why: The same underflow under the asymmetric formula, where the range rather than the magnitude is subnormal.
refusals.detail: subnormal_scale_int4_asymmetric derived scale 0.0, which is not a normal f32; quantising it would divide by zero or emit infinities

refusals.name: constant_subnormal_int4_asymmetric
refusals.why: A CONSTANT subnormal unit. Under s = |c| the scale is the subnormal itself, so §3.1's existing subnormal-scale row refuses it -- which is what symmetric already did with the same input. Under the s = 1 rule it silently reconstructed to 0.0.
refusals.detail: constant_subnormal_int4_asymmetric derived scale 1.401298464324817e-45, which is not a normal f32; quantising it would divide by zero or emit infinities

refusals.name: constant_subnormal_int4_symmetric
refusals.why: The symmetric counterpart, which refuses on the same row: s = max|g|/7 underflows to zero.
refusals.detail: constant_subnormal_int4_symmetric derived scale 0.0, which is not a normal f32; quantising it would divide by zero or emit infinities

refusals.name: nan_in_unit_int8_symmetric
refusals.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 5: refused, and the refusal names the tensor. A non-finite weight is a finding, reported as one.
refusals.detail: nan_in_unit_int8_symmetric holds a non-finite value at index 1; non-finite weights are a finding, not something to quantise

refusals.name: positive_infinity_in_unit_int8_asymmetric
refusals.why: +Inf is refused on the same rule as NaN rather than propagating through max() into an infinite scale.
refusals.detail: positive_infinity_in_unit_int8_asymmetric holds a non-finite value at index 1; non-finite weights are a finding, not something to quantise

refusals.name: negative_infinity_in_unit_int4_symmetric
refusals.detail: negative_infinity_in_unit_int4_symmetric holds a non-finite value at index 0; non-finite weights are a finding, not something to quantise

refusals.name: reconstruction_overflows_to_infinity_int8_symmetric
refusals.why: A constant unit at f32::MAX under int8 symmetric. The scale is normal (f32::MAX/127) and every input is finite, but 127*s rounds UP past f32::MAX, so the reconstruction overflows. §3.1: never silently produce infinities -- so it is refused, naming the unit and the offending index. Note this is the RECONSTRUCTION overflowing, not the scale: `scale_overflows_to_infinity_...` below is the other case.
refusals.detail: reconstruction_overflows_to_infinity_int8_symmetric reconstructs to a non-finite value at index 0: code 127 times scale 2.6793887059314005e+36 overflows f32. Refused rather than emitted

refusals.name: reconstruction_overflows_to_infinity_negative_int8_symmetric
refusals.why: The same overflow with the sign flipped, so -Inf is refused too rather than only +Inf.
refusals.detail: reconstruction_overflows_to_infinity_negative_int8_symmetric reconstructs to a non-finite value at index 0: code -127 times scale 2.6793887059314005e+36 overflows f32. Refused rather than emitted

refusals.name: reconstruction_overflows_from_supplied_params_int4_symmetric
refusals.why: The same refusal reached with params supplied rather than derived, which is the per-tensor and per-channel case. s = 2e38 and x = f32::MAX give rint(1.7014) = 2, and 2*s = 4e38 overflows. A scale of f32::MAX itself would NOT reach this: every finite input then rounds to code 0 and reconstructs to 0.0.
refusals.detail: reconstruction_overflows_from_supplied_params_int4_symmetric reconstructs to a non-finite value at index 0: code 2 times scale 1.9999999360571385e+38 overflows f32. Refused rather than emitted

refusals.name: scale_overflows_to_infinity_int8_asymmetric
refusals.why: max - min overflows f32 to +Inf, so the scale is not finite. §3.1: never silently produce infinities.
refusals.detail: scale_overflows_to_infinity_int8_asymmetric derived scale inf, which is not a normal f32; quantising it would divide by zero or emit infinities

refusals.name: zero_point_outside_i32_int8_asymmetric
refusals.why: A huge offset with a one-ULP range: lo = -1e30 and hi its neighbour toward zero, so s = ulp(1e30)/255 = 2.96e20 and z = rint(1e30/s) = 3374896640, outside i32 (max 2147483647). Refused rather than wrapped. Not a constant unit: constants are exactly representable under the s = |c| rule and no longer reach this path.
refusals.detail: zero_point_outside_i32_int8_asymmetric needs zero point 3374896640, which is outside i32

refusals.name: empty_unit_int8_symmetric
refusals.why: An empty unit has no max and no range; refused rather than returning a fabricated scale.
refusals.detail: empty_unit_int8_symmetric is empty; there is nothing to quantise

refusals.name: non_finite_reaches_simulate_int8_symmetric
refusals.why: Non-finite values are refused in simulate too, not only in derive_params -- params may have been derived from another unit.
refusals.detail: non_finite_reaches_simulate_int8_symmetric holds a non-finite value at index 1; non-finite weights are a finding, not something to quantise

refusals.name: subnormal_scale_reaches_simulate_int8_symmetric
refusals.why: A subnormal scale handed to simulate is refused rather than dividing by something that underflows.
refusals.detail: subnormal_scale_reaches_simulate_int8_symmetric derived scale 1.401298464324817e-45, which is not a normal f32; quantising it would divide by zero or emit infinities

refusals.name: zero_scale_reaches_simulate_int8_symmetric
refusals.why: Division by a zero scale is refused, not attempted.
refusals.detail: zero_scale_reaches_simulate_int8_symmetric derived scale 0.0, which is not a normal f32; quantising it would divide by zero or emit infinities

refusals.name: symmetric_with_non_zero_zero_point
refusals.why: A symmetric config carries no zero point; a non-zero one is an inconsistent parameter pair and is refused before any arithmetic.
refusals.detail: symmetric_with_non_zero_zero_point is symmetric, so its zero point must be 0, not 3

refusals.name: group_size_zero
refusals.why: Group size 0 would produce no groups; refused at validation.
refusals.detail: group size 0 would produce no groups
